title: Why Montecucco Sangiovese tastes the way it does

lede.text: Montecucco Sangiovese comes from vineyards of at least 90% Sangiovese in seven communes of Grosseto province.

chapters.title: Seven communes in Grosseto
paras: The grapes come from vineyards in seven communes of the province of Grosseto. The zone covers land suited to quality and to growing vines.

chapters.title: Sangiovese, with a little room
paras: Montecucco Sangiovese is made from red grapes only. Each estate's vineyards must hold at least 90% Sangiovese.
Up to 10% can be other red grapes that are suited to growing in Tuscany. Three are excluded: both Malvasia Nera types and Aleatico.
The name can carry the word riserva. The Sangiovese minimum stays at 90%.
The wine was approved as a DOC in 1998 and became a DOCG in 2011.
